endpoint_inventory: https://connect-gw-coral.umos.ai (coral env, hardcoded baseURL in CCGAuthenticator)

findings.title: generateDeterministicPrivateKey: passphrase → single SHA-256 → ECC private key (no PBKDF2 / Argon2 / salt / iterations)
findings.rationale: Deriving an ECC private key from a passphrase via a single SHA-256 hash exposes weak passphrases to cheap brute-force. There is no salt and no iteration count, so identical passphrases always produce identical keys; an attacker who guesses the passphrase recovers every derived key for every device. Standard practice is PBKDF2 / scrypt / Argon2 with a per-device salt and a high iteration / cost parameter.

findings.title: Kotlin data-class auto-generated toString() embeds the authenticator token
findings.rationale: If any caller logs an AuthData instance (Timber, Log.d, exception messages, Result.toString), the access token leaks into logcat. The hosting APK has INTERNET, RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED, GET_ACCOUNTS, QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES — it is exactly the kind of background sync service whose token would unlock backend access. Any other privileged process that reads logcat (or a `dumpsys logd` privileged user) sees the token. Mitigation: override toString() to mask the token, or strip the token field from the data-class footprint.

findings.title: Hardcoded production endpoint + clientID/clientSecret are sent over an HttpClient with no visible certificate pinning at this layer
findings.rationale: TLS scheme is used (https://). However: (1) the production endpoint is hardcoded — environment changes require re-shipping the APK; (2) this class issues a POST to `${baseURL}/auth/client/login` carrying `client_id` and `secret`. There is no certificate-pinning configuration in this file. If pinning is not configured at the shared HttpClient layer (CCGTokenProvider / network-security-config / OkHttp interceptor), a MITM with a trusted CA harvests the client credentials. Follow-up to confirm pinning is the next stage-2 step.

results.discovered_during: Phase B-3.c follow-up (HMGAuthenticator read while resolving ssl-3 pinning)

findings.title: HmgUserInfo data-class toString() embeds driver PII (UUID, birthdate, email, name)
findings.rationale: Same Kotlin data-class auto-toString pattern as ssl-2 (AuthData) but for driver PII rather than just an opaque token. If any caller logs HmgUserInfo (Timber, Log.d, exception, Result.toString), full driver identity (UUID + birthdate + email + name) reaches logcat. logcat is readable by READ_LOGS / dumpsys / vendor diagnostics. Severity HIGH (PII regulatory impact + identity theft surface).

findings.title: BuildConfig.IDENTIFIER used as ECC KDF passphrase — build-time constant baked into the APK
findings.rationale: BuildConfig.IDENTIFIER is a build-time constant baked into every APK by the Android Gradle plugin. Combined with the deterministic SHA-256 KDF in ECCCrypto.generateDeterministicPrivateKey, every device derives the same ECC private key from this constant. APK reverse engineering trivially recovers BuildConfig → recovers the key → decrypts every device's encryptedYaml config (server endpoints + secrets). Independent finding from ssl-1 (which is the KDF design issue); this finding is the hardcoded-secret root cause that makes ssl-1 exploitable.

results.discovered_during: Phase B-3.c grep for log emission

findings.title: gRPC sync channel uses .usePlaintext() — TLS off, vehicle syslog sent in cleartext
findings.rationale: B-3.c 추가 grep 결과 SysLogService:76에서 io.grpc.ManagedChannelBuilder의 `.usePlaintext()` 명시적 호출 confirmed. TLS 없이 gRPC frame 평문 전송 → MITM (corporate proxy / hostile Wi-Fi / network tap)이 차량 systemID + 진단 페이로드 평문 관찰. line 120의 'connect-gw.umos.ai:9091' Log.i와 결합 시 endpoint 노출도 추가. CCGAuthenticator (HTTPS) 와 SysLogService (gRPC plaintext) 는 별도 channel — sync 패키지의 두 channel 중 syslog 가 평문.
